questions.question: _____ in Gujarat was the emporium of western trade during the Mughal Period.
questions.solution:
• Mughal Emporium: Surat
  • Fact: During the Mughal era, Surat was the gate to Mecca and the most vital port for trade with West Asia and Europe.

questions.question: ho wrote the book ‘Gulamgiri’?
questions.solution:
• Gulamgiri Author: Jyotirao Phule
  • 1873: Phule wrote this book (meaning 'Slavery') and dedicated it to the American movement to free slaves.

questions.question: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi arrive in India from South Africa?
questions.solution:
• Gandhi's Arrival: 1915
  • Detail: Mahatma Gandhi returned from South Africa on 9 January 1915, a day now celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

questions.question: Megasthenes, an ambassador, was sent to the court of ______ by the Greek ruler of West Asia, Seleucus Nicator.
questions.solution:
• Megasthenes' Visit: Chandragupta
  • Note: He was the Greek ambassador of Seleucus Nicator and wrote the famous account 'Indica' about the Mauryan Empire.

questions.question: Who among the following Mughal rulers built the Agra Fort?
questions.solution:
• Agra Fort Builder: Akbar
  • Architecture: While Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal, Akbar was responsible for the massive red sandstone Agra Fort (1565–1573).

questions.question: In a freestanding temple, the mountain-like spire, which can take the shape of a pyramidal tower is called _________.
questions.solution:
• Vimana: vimana
  • Temple Style: In Dravidian (South Indian) architecture, the pyramidal tower over the sanctum is called the Vimana.

questions.question: Quit India movement was started in ______.
questions.solution:
• Quit India Movement: 1942
  • Slogan: Launched at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee with the call 'Do or Die'.

questions.question: Which freedom fighter is also known as the ‘Grand Old Man of lndia’?
questions.solution:
• Grand Old Man: Dadabhai Naoroji
  • Achievement: He was a founding member of the INC and the first Indian to be a British Member of Parliament.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Mauryan ruler who tried to spread his message to the people through inscriptions?
questions.solution:
• Ashokan Inscriptions: Ashoka
  • Detail: He was the first ruler to use stone pillars and rock edicts to communicate 'Dhamma' to his subjects in Prakrit and Greek.

questions.question: ueen Rudramadevi belonged to which dynasty of India?
questions.solution:
• Rudramadevi: Kakatiya
  • History: One of the few ruling queens in Indian history, she ruled the Kakatiya dynasty from Orugallu (modern Warangal).

questions.question: ____________, popularly known as Punjab Kesari took his last breath on November 17th, 1928
questions.solution:
• Punjab Kesari: Lala Lajpat Rai
  • Martyrdom: He died in 1928 after being severely injured during a lathi charge while protesting the Simon Commission.

questions.question:
Which of the following pair of ‘Name of Ruler - Empire’ is correctly matched?
I. Mahapadma Nanda - Magadha Empire
II. Ajatasattu - Maurya Empire
questions.solution:
• Ruler-Empire Match: Only I
  • Correction: Mahapadma Nanda ruled Magadha (Correct). Ajatasattu belonged to the Haryanka dynasty, not the Maurya dynasty (Incorrect).

questions.question: When Alivardi Khan died in 1756, ______ became the nawab of Bengal.
questions.solution:
• Bengal Nawab (1756): Siraj-ud-daulah
  • Succession: He succeeded his grandfather Alivardi Khan and eventually fought the British at the Battle of Plassey.

questions.question: hich of the following is also known as ‘New Stone Age’ in the civilisation history of India?
questions.solution:
• New Stone Age: Neolithic
  • Era: Characterized by the beginning of agriculture, animal domestication, and polished stone tools.

questions.question: ho among the following British Viceroys partitioned Bengal in 1905?
questions.solution:
• Bengal Partition (1905): Lord Curzon
  • Impact: The partition triggered the Swadeshi Movement and widespread anti-British protests.

questions.question: Sayyid Ahmed Khan founded Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College in _________ in 1875.
questions.solution:
• Aligarh Movement: Aligarh
  • MAO College: Founded in 1875 by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, it later became the Aligarh Muslim University (AMU).

questions.question: The revenue system of Mughal period during Akbar’s reign was called ______.
questions.solution:
• Zabt System: Zabt
  • Revenue: Introduced by Raja Todar Mal, it involved land measurement and fixed tax based on average produce of the last 10 years.
